Title: Procedures for ambient-pressure and tympanometric tests of aural acoustic reflectance and admittance in human infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: wideband acoustic reflectance/admittance measurement (ambient pressure and tympanometric)
Outcome: Procedures described; infant absorbance peaks aligned in frequency with group-delay dips (canal-wall mobility model)
Evidence_Quote: Procedures are described to measure acoustic reflectance and admittance in human adult and infant ears at frequencies from 0.2 to 8 kHz.

Title: Optimizing swept-tone protocols for recording distortion-product otoacoustic emissions in adults and newborns.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: distortion-product otoacoustic emissions
Evidence_Quote: In this study, the optimal parameters (i.e., sweep rate and duration of the LSF analysis window) required to record and analyze swept-tone DPOAEs were tested and defined in 15 adults and 10 newborns.

Title: Explaining the high voice superiority effect in polyphonic music: evidence from cortical evoked potentials and peripheral auditory models.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: polyphonic music; two simultaneous voices; deviant pitches
Outcome: cortical evoked potentials; encoding of higher versus lower voice
Evidence_Quote: Furthermore, infants also show this high-voice superiority effect, suggesting that the perceptual dominance observed across studies might result from neurophysiological characteristics of the peripheral auditory system.

Title: The impact of cesarean section on neonatal outcome of infants born at 23weeks of gestation.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: infants born at 23 weeks of gestation; infants born at 24-26 weeks
Outcome: neonatal death; cerebral palsy; poor neonatal outcome
Evidence_Quote: Poor outcome included neonatal death or cerebral palsy.

Title: Infant sleep machines and hazardous sound pressure levels.
Journal: Pediatrics
Outcome: maximum output sound pressure levels; risk of noise-induced hearing loss; uninterrupted sleep
Evidence_Quote: Infant "sleep machines" (ISMs) produce ambient noise or noise to mask other sounds in an infant's room with the goal of increasing uninterrupted sleep.

Title: Early exposure to maternal voice: effects on preterm infants development.
Journal: Early human development
Stimulus_Type: maternal voice administered by bone conduction
Outcome: heart rate; stable skin color; visual attention; quality of general movements; neurofunctional assessment; autonomic and neurobehavioral development
Evidence_Quote: To investigate the effect of the exposure to maternal voice, administered by bone conduction, on preterm infants autonomic and neurobehavioral development.

Title: Vowel discrimination by hearing infants as a function of number of spectral channels.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: vowel discrimination; looking time
Evidence_Quote: This study assessed impact of number of spectral channels on vowel discrimination by 6-month-old infants with normal hearing by comparing three listening conditions: Unprocessed speech, 32 channels, and 16 channels.

Title: On the rhythm of infant- versus adult-directed speech in Australian English.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: rhythmic differences; durational measures; prominence of vocalic/sonorant segments; pitch
Evidence_Quote: The findings are reported of an investigation into rhythmic differences between infant-directed speech (IDS) and adult-directed speech (ADS) in a corpus of utterances from Australian English mothers speaking to their infants and to another adult.

Title: Perception of the pitch of unresolved harmonics by 3- and 7-month-old human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: missing-fundamental harmonic complexes (unresolved harmonics), bandpass filtered, with pink noise
Outcome: Nearly all infants categorized complexes by MF pitch (discrimination of unresolved harmonics by 3 months)
Evidence_Quote: Stimuli were MF complexes bandpass filtered with a -12 dB/octave slope, combined in random phase, presented at 70 dB sound pressure level (SPL) for 650 ms with a 50 ms rise/fall with a pink noise at 65 dB SPL. The conditions were (1) "LOW" unresolved harmonics (2500-4500 Hz) based on MFs of 160 and 200 Hz and (2) "HIGH" unresolved harmonics (4000-6000 Hz) based on MFs of 190 and 200 Hz.

Title: Preliminary evaluation of a two-interval, two-alternative infant behavioral testing procedure.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: detection criterion (80% correct) achieved by 10 of 11 infants in a single session
Evidence_Quote: Ten of 11 infants (7-9 months of age) achieved a criterion of 80%-correct detection of a 50-dB sound pressure level noise band in a single testing session.

Title: Maternal sounds elicit lower heart rate in preterm newborns in the first month of life.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: preterm infants born between 25 and 32 weeks of gestation
Outcome: heart rate
Evidence_Quote: Heart rate changes were monitored in 20 hospitalized preterm infants born between 25 and 32 weeks of gestation during 30-minute exposure vs. non-exposure periods of recorded maternal sounds played inside the incubator.

Title: The acoustic properties of bilingual infant-directed speech.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: acoustic characteristics of point vowels
Evidence_Quote: The acoustic characteristics of the point vowels /a,i,u/ were measured in the spontaneous infant-directed speech of French-English bilingual mothers, as well as in the speech of French and English monolingual mothers.

Title: Distortion-product otoacoustic emission reflection-component delays and cochlear tuning: estimates from across the human lifespan.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 184 subjects from prematurely born neonates to elderly adults
Stimulus_Type: distortion-product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAE at 2f1-f2), reflection component
Outcome: Reflection-component delays estimated across lifespan; term newborns showed longest delays and sharpest tuning
Evidence_Quote: DPOAEs were measured from 0.5-4 kHz in all age groups and extended to 8 kHz in young adults.

Title: Kangaroo care: cardio-respiratory relationships between the infant and caregiver.
Journal: Early human development
Stimulus_Type: skin-to-skin contact (kangaroo care) vs incubator control
Outcome: During SSC, infant respiratory instability and apnea related to caregiver heart rate variance; cardio-respiratory coupling enhanced in eupneic frequency range
Evidence_Quote: Infant cardio-respiratory coupling was also enhanced during SSC compared to CTL in the eupneic frequency range (0.7-1.5 Hz, p=0.018) and reduced for slower frequencies (0.15-0.45 Hz; p=0.036).

Title: Expressive timing in infant-directed singing between 3 and 6 months.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Stimulus_Type: maternal infant-directed singing; popular French playsong
Outcome: expressive timing of maternal singing
Evidence_Quote: To this end, the interactions of 18 mother-infant dyads were recorded while mothers were singing a popular French playsong for their infant at 3 and then at 6 months.

Title: Maturation of the human medial efferent reflex revisited.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: premature and term-born neonates, 6-month-old infants, and young adults
Stimulus_Type: contralateral acoustic stimulation (CAS) during DPOAE recording
Outcome: MOC reflex strongest at frequencies below 1.5 kHz for all ages; maturation likely prior to full-term birth
Evidence_Quote: For all ages, the MOC reflex was strongest at frequencies below 1.5 kHz, and the reflection component of the DPOAE was most affected, showing maximally reduced amplitude and shallower phase slope when contralateral noise was presented.

Title: Gender-specific heart rate dynamics in severe intrauterine growth-restricted fetuses.
Journal: Early human development
Outcome: fetal heart rate dynamics; mean fetal heart rate; entropy
Evidence_Quote: FHR was analyzed in the antepartum period in 15 severe IUGR fetuses and 18 controls, matched for gestational age, in relation to fetal gender.

Title: Parental psychological distress during pregnancy and childhood cardiovascular development. The Generation R Study.
Journal: Early human development
Outcome: blood pressure; carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity; left ventricular mass; fractional shortening
Evidence_Quote: At the child age of six years, we performed blood pressure and carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity measurements, and M-mode measurements of left cardiac structures and fractional shortening.

Title: The effects of music therapy on vital signs, feeding, and sleep in premature infants.
Journal: Pediatrics
Stimulus_Type: live music; parent-preferred lullabies; rhythm; entrained breath sounds
Outcome: heart rate; respiratory rates; O2 saturation; sleep; feeding behavior; sucking behavior; caloric intake; parental stress perception
Evidence_Quote: The live elements of music such as rhythm, breath, and parent-preferred lullabies may affect physiologic function (eg, heart and respiratory rates, O2 saturation levels, and activity levels) and developmental function (eg, sleep, feeding behavior, and weight gain) in premature infants.

Title: Infants' name recognition in on- and off-channel noise.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: effect of maskers on attention to target frequency range
Evidence_Quote: The current study explores this effect of irrelevant distractors further and finds that 8-month-old infants are significantly less affected by maskers outside the frequency range (off-channel maskers) than by on-channel maskers.

Title: Infants' detection and discrimination of sounds in modulated maskers.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: sounds in modulated maskers; vowel; tone
Outcome: vowel discrimination; tone detection
Evidence_Quote: Adults and 7-month-old infants were compared in detection and discrimination of sounds in modulated maskers.
